title: Warband of Valhalla - Steam Page live! So excited. Thank goodness for AI art.
author: Practical-Raccoon-88
selftext:
Hi guys, made this game relatively quicky(about 8 months) with the use of AI for animations, art, UI and so on.

I did all the coding myself.

  
[Warband of Valhalla](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5294780/Warband_Of_Valhalla/) \- Steam page.  
Make the perfect Viking kill Squad by training each different skills. There is perma-death, so be careful which battles you take on. Send them on missions to obtain loot.

Upgrade your blacksmith for better gear.

I used local QWEN2511 model on Comfyui to make the characters, enemies and loot/gear. ChatGPT for UI, QWEN2511 was also used to make animation sprite sheets. I would make about 10 walking animation sprite sheets, then copy them all into one big Aseprite worksheet, then select the best sprites that form the smoothest animation for each character. 

  
Some of the animations was done with Grok making a small video of it walking/attacking/dying, then i just run it in a website to break it down into frames, remove background and import to game.

replies.author: Johny-115
replies.body:
i am really considering trying my luck at game dev too .. its just ... ai or not .. it takes time .. sure its not 5 years anymore as solo dev to make nice game, its maybe 6 months (i hope) .. but thats still a lot of fucking time

that said, i did some experiments already .. and i dont know why people keep making sloppy AI games ... Opus 5.5 makes it so easy ... pixel art and even animations Opus 5.5 can do from scratch look really good ... the problem with using image models, well first, slop devs just use chatgpt, which is really bad and recognizable, second, it introduces so many problems and complications to use it tastefully .. it only works for certain type of games where the images are really not animated much, and even then, problem to keep consistency and whatno

replies.author: Johny-115
replies.body:
why would it not work?

i made a pixelart street fighter with dozens of unique characters and stages, each with unique ultimates ... everything in the stage backgrounds moves too

and experimenting with dungeon crawler game now

it rigs the characters, does any animation needed

for example: in the image lower, the wolf death animation looked wonky for example, but the version C made it so that it looks very natural .. doesnt look like rigged shapes but the wolf folds .. characters are also animted to breathe, walk, attack, take damage, etc.

all vanila Opus 5.5, no skills

sure if youd compare to sprites of actual street fighter, then no ... thats totally different level ... but as for the dungeon crawler lower, most of my reference games i love, look a lot worse, they buy sprite packs and then dont do any animations, because its just not feasible for solo dev games pre-AI, they were great games due to gameplay mechanics and content, well, now you can have unique animations for hundreds of enemy types, etc. .. i am using 24px tiles tiles and at least within that style, it doesnt look sloppy to me

at least my ambition isnt to surpass the most artistic pixel art games loved by millions, thats all hand-drawn magic ... surpassing smaller solo-dev indie games that bought sprite packs or cut corners for their own sanity, is possible though, at least in the visuals .. i think

THE only test is ... does Opus 5.5 animated pixel art look better and less sloppy then badly animated ChatGPT image bitmaps? to me thats a yes .. that was my whole point ... not that Opus 5.5 can rival something like Slay the Spire 2 ..... something like Stardew Valley ... with lot of effort .. wouldnt be so sure it cant though, think it could get quite close, with lot of referencing and massive amount of tweaking .. and Stardew Valley is considered peak pixelart success
